scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of the default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy. The repo is a single PostGIS SQL script (ObsToEvents.sql) plus a README, a sample shapefile (vertices.*) and images; SQL is outside the supported Python/Node scope of skill version 1.0, so the script was read in full and only deps, config, secrets patterns, hosts and DDL/DML operations were inventoried. There is no application code, no Python or Node files, and no database connection setup.

entry_points.framework: PostgreSQL/PostGIS (run manually in psql or a SQL client)

databases.credential_source: none in repo (script contains no connection string; the operator's own client session supplies credentials)

sql_injection_risk.reason: static DDL/DML script with no dynamic SQL or user input; schema name 'greatpond' is hardcoded in every statement

file_system_access.detail: sample point shapefile (with .dbf, .shx, .prj, .cpg, .qmd) committed as data

what_this_app_can_do: Creates an observations table (greatpond.obs: name, desc, severity_int, size, point geometry in EPSG:6348) and a GIST index in a PostGIS database.
Matches each observation point to its nearest trail line within 200 m and computes its linear-referencing measure along the trail, then builds events, event_points and segments tables.
Drops and recreates the output tables greatpond.events, greatpond.event_points and greatpond.segments each time it is run (DROP TABLE IF EXISTS).

data_sources_touched.source: PostgreSQL/PostGIS schema 'greatpond': tables obs (input), trails (input), events, event_points, segments (outputs)
sample shapefile vertices.shp in the repo

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Not a running service: the script is executed manually by someone who already has database access. Access is governed entirely by the PostgreSQL role used, which is not specified in the repo.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: Script drops and recreates tables in schema 'greatpond' without confirmation (destructive if the same names are used elsewhere)
No role or privilege handling is defined in the script

top_findings: No secrets, credentials, hosts or code beyond one SQL script
Script uses DROP TABLE IF EXISTS on output tables in a hardcoded schema
No dependency manifest or deployment documentation (none applicable)
